rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This tests a simple RNA-only model with PCA encoding and singleprofile, isolating the RNA modality's performance. It clarifies the baseline accuracy for RNA data, which is critical for comparing multimodal or image-only models later.

The existing evidence shows that using singleprofile with pca_n2000 gives 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with the same RNA encoder but avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting. It balances exploration (testing multiprofile) and exploitation (keeping RNA encoder and image settings consistent) to determine if profile setting impacts performance.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) for RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (config_002) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of multiprofile's advantage with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation), prioritizing uncertainty reduction about critical components.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.590664 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and transformer aggregation variants. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) improves performance while keeping multiprofile and avgpool settings consistent. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, which is critical for determining if advanced encoders can surpass simpler ones in this context.

The existing evidence shows that config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.650). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only configuration, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation (building on a proven RNA encoder/aggregation) and exploration (testing multimodal potential), which is critical given remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests adding a strong image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) to the multimodal setting while retaining the proven RNA encoder and aggregation method. It isolates the impact of the image encoder's quality, which could potentially boost performance without complicating other factors. This balances exploration of multimodal benefits with leveraging established effective components.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_036) achieves high accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (instead of concat) with resnet50 image encoder (config_037) could improve performance. It isolates the effect of fusion method while keeping RNA encoder consistent, providing insight into whether weighted fusion is beneficial for resnet50. This balances exploitation of the scvi_n200 RNA encoder's strength with exploration of fusion methods, maximizing the chance of finding a better configuration within the remaining budget.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and concat fusion achieve high accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_036) with transformer aggregation to determine if it improves performance. Since aggregation methods significantly impact model performance, this comparison clarifies whether transformer aggregation offers better representation learning for multimodal data, while keeping other components (RNA encoder, image encoder, fusion) consistent.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_038: 0.7207 accuracy) outperform other settings. This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the same configuration could further improve accuracy. It isolates the effect of fusion method, which is critical for multimodal performance, and leverages the strong foundation of the current top-performing setup.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l and transformer aggregation/weighted fusion (config_039) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests whether the scgpt RNA encoder (a new encoder not yet tested in multimodal settings) could further improve performance when paired with the best image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and fusion strategy. It directly addresses uncertainty about the RNA encoder's impact on multimodal performance, leveraging prior success of the image encoder and fusion method.
